title: Rome disputes in vain as if Reformed put faith in notitia and exact science
source_text: LXIII. Itaque frustra disputant Ecclesiae Romanae Doctores contra Reformatae Scholae Theologos, quasi fidem non tam in assensu, quam in notitia rei creditae constituant. Item quasi ad fidem singulorum requirant exactam, accuratam, & distinctam cognitionem mysteriorum fidei, per quam aliquis illa explicare, tueri ac defendere possit; ut tenetur facere Doctor aliquis, & Verbi Divini Minister.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore the Doctors of the Roman Church dispute in vain against the theologians of the Reformed school as if they constituted faith not so much in assent as in knowledge of the thing believed; likewise as if for the faith of individuals they required an exact, accurate, and distinct cognition of the mysteries of faith by which someone can explain, defend, and protect them, as some Doctor and Minister of the Divine Word is bound to do.
pass_b_english: Rome argues in vain as if Reformed located faith in notitia rather than assent, and as if every believer must have exact accurate distinct cognition able to explain and defend mysteries like a doctor or minister.

lemmas.latin: non tam in assensu, quam in notitia
lemmas.gloss: not so much in assent as in knowledge

rejected: Reformed demand theologian-level knowledge of all
